note: Item text: German MABS wording (Wittich, Hansche, Knappe & Martini 2009) verbatim from the study's own S1 File (journal.pone.0316374.s001.docx, CC BY 4.0), parsed from document.xml: instructions from the text box, 19 stems from Word numbered list numId 2 (decimal '%1.', one continuous list 1..19; item 1's stem is split over two paragraphs and was joined with a space), 95 options from the bullet list numId 1 in document order, 5 per item. Source spellings kept as printed ('Babies', 'in meinen Bauch'). Codes: the processing script pivots the S2 .xlsx column names unchanged (maas_<N>[r]_t<k>); the .xlsx carries no labels, so the tie code->text is the item number N in the column name matched to the S1 numbered list (paper_explicit). Verified against Table 2 (t002 image): all 19 T1 items reproduce the published M/SD/skewness/kurtosis exactly. resp: Condon's scoring key (Flinders PDF: 'Items in brackets are reversed scored. Scoring is 1-5, with 5 high attachment'; brackets on 1,3,5,6,7,9,10,12,15,16,18) matches the r-suffixed columns exactly, and Table 2 footnote says reverse-coded items are stored so higher = higher attachment; so for r items resp 5 = first-listed option, for the rest resp 1 = first-listed option. All corrected item-total r at wave 0 are positive (0.18-0.53). English (_translated): Condon's own English MAAS (Flinders Academic Commons hdl 2328/35292, bitstream sha256 518648400e03697be4db3ea47b38747d9ca07bba2630cfe031054f13b80fe44b) for the same numbered items, not a translation of the German; the German instructions add a third sentence ('Es gibt keine richtigen oder falschen Antworten.') that the English original lacks, and minor wording differs (e.g. item 13 German 'gegenüber meinem Baby' vs English options carrying 'emotionally ... my baby'). Rights: originator page states 'This is an Open Access article distributed under the terms of the Creative Commons Attribution License 3.0 AU ... which permits unrestricted use, distribution, and reproduction in any medium, provided the original work is properly cited.' and each page 'This work is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 Australian license (CC BY 3.0 AU).' No fee, permission, NC, ND or no-redistribution clause on the MAAS or on the German S1 (footer is a bare copyright notice). Not in instrument_rights_register.csv (the register's MAAS rows are the Mindful Attention Awareness Scale, a different instrument). Ships. t2 codes (maas_2,4,8,11,13,14,17,19 _t2) carry the same text as their _t1 twins; Table 2 is T1-only so their mapping rests on the column-name number (cross-wave r picks the same-number T1 item for 6 of 8; 13 and 19 are ceiling items). RESPONSE-DATA DEFECT (not an item-text problem): in the live table every reverse-keyed item (maas_1r,3r,5r,6r,7r,9r,10r,12r,15r,16r,18r) has 368 rows = 184 at wave 0 plus 184 at wave 1, and all 2024/2024 wave-1 rows are identical (same id, item, resp) to the wave-0 rows. Cause: data/rvobgvmaas_lsf_lehing_2024.r builds maas_t2r_df with ends_with("t1") instead of ends_with("t2"), so T1 reverse-item responses were relabelled as wave 1 and the source's 11 maas_*r_t2 columns never reached IRW (they differ from T1, e.g. maas_12r_t2 mean 4.89 range 1-5 vs maas_12r_t1 4.88 range 2-5; maas_18r_t2 4.96 vs 4.72). Fix: change ends_with("t1") to ends_with("t2") in the maas_t2r_df block and re-upload; the item codes would then be maas_<N>r_t2 at wave 1 and this itemtext would need those 11 codes added (same text as the _t1 rows).
public_note: Items are shown in the administered German (Wittich et al. 2009) with Condon's original English alongside, which is the source instrument rather than a translation of the German. In the response table, the wave-1 rows for the 11 reverse-keyed items (codes ending r_t1) are copies of the wave-0 rows (2024 of 2024 identical) because of a processing-script error, so the study's T2 answers to those items are not in IRW.
